title: Uncertainty Elicitation as an Oversight Signal: Teaching Strong Models to Flag What Weak Overseers Cannot Verify

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: If models can identify their own oversight-resistant outputs, this creates a practical tool for improving oversight pipelines. Direct safety relevance: flagging unverifiable outputs prevents undetected failures.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Training a model to output overseer-verifiability scores requires designing the training signal, creating a dataset of verifiable/unverifiable outputs, and training a multi-output model. This is conceptually sophisticated and technically demanding for beginners.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Multiple interacting components: defining verifiability, generating training data for verifiability scores, training the multi-output model, and evaluating whether scores predict overseer accuracy. Too many moving parts for 30 hours.

novelty_assessment.reasoning: Novelty not assessed due to partial Wave 3 completion.
